solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Obvious curse coming with dismissal of second worker

indicators.note: dismissal sends something away, so a letter is removed from the curse word

parts.note: to curse is to blast, as in 'blast it!'
the ant is the crossword's usual worker insect

explanation.surface: A manager swears openly after sacking an assistant who was the second hand on the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismissal of second' takes S out of BLAST, leaving BLAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: something flagrant and unconcealed is plainly visible to all.

clue.text: Children originally exposed in lark possibly given old-fashioned punishment?

indicators.note: in places the children and first letter inside the bird

parts.note: a lark is one example of a bird
ch. is the abbreviation for children, as in reference books

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of exposed

explanation.surface: Kids caught out in a prank are given a caning, as in the old days.
explanation.definitionFit: Beating with a bundle of twigs was a traditional school or judicial penalty.

clue.text: Vegetable not favoured in foreign inn

indicators.note: not says the favoured letters are left out of the vegetable

parts.note: aubergine is the British name for eggplant
to be in is to be in favour or fashionable

explanation.surface: An out-of-favour vegetable dish served at an inn abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Auberge is the French word for an inn or hostelry, used in English too.

clue.text: Maiden entering was drunk in a banquet — but not from this!

indicators.note: in places the maiden and drunk letters within the banquet

parts.note: to dine is to feast, so dine stands for banquet

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so the maiden goes into the drunk letters
drunk suggests letters reeling about, so they are rearranged

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A girl got tipsy at a feast, though not on the water.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a jokey twist: the girl was drunk at a banquet, so she cannot have been drinking water.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam's wine is a jocular name for water, the only drink the first man had.

clue.text: Chinese food with distinctive flavour served outside theatre

indicators.note: served outside means placed around, so the flavour wraps the theatre

parts.note: a tang is a sharp, distinctive taste
rep is a repertory theatre

explanation.surface: A tasty Chinese dish is dished up outside a playhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea cucumber, dried and eaten as a delicacy in Chinese cuisine.

clue.text: Like many a gun named out loud

indicators.note: said out loud tells us to listen to the word rather than read it

parts.note: to be named in a report is to be cited

explanation.surface: A firearm is named in public, as at a trial or in a report.
explanation.definitionFit: Most rifles and pistols carry sights for aiming, so they are fitted with them.

clue.text: Various eagles seen around north country

indicators.note: seen around means encircling, so the shuffled birds go round the north letter
various means differing in arrangement, so the letters are shuffled

parts.note: N is the compass abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: Different eagles are spotted roaming about a northern land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Various' rearranges EAGLES into SENEGAL less the N, which goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation on the west coast of Africa, capital Dakar.

clue.text: Little urchin playin' competitively

definitions.meaning: gambling or competing, with the dropped g shown by the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A small street kid plays games, dropping his g's.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamin is a neglected street child; gamin' is gaming with the final letter clipped.

clue.text: Expression briefly used to encapsulate wine that's more palatable

indicators.note: to encapsulate is to enclose, so the shortened expression goes round the wine
briefly means cut short, losing the last letter

parts.note: a term is a word or expression
Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

explanation.surface: A short phrase is used to describe a better-tasting wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' trims TERM to TER, which holds ASTI.
explanation.definitionFit: A comparative: more flavourful, nicer to eat or drink.

clue.text: Lots of papers one left out for tramps?

indicators.note: left out means omitted, so the one letter is removed

parts.note: a dossier is a file of papers; dossiers are lots of them
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Bundles of documents, one left out on the street for vagrants.
explanation.definitionFit: Doss is slang for sleeping rough, so dossers are homeless vagrants.

clue.text: Anger about one in a previous era — where did that woman originally come from?!

definitions.text: where did that woman originally come from

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the anger word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: rage is fierce anger
the Roman numeral I is one
BC, before Christ, marks the era before the present one

explanation.surface: Someone, furious at a long-ago age, wonders aloud about a woman's origins.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis Eve was made from Adam's rib, so 'that woman' came from inside the rib cage.
explanation.definitionFit: A biblical allusion: Eve was fashioned from one of Adam's ribs, housed in his chest.

clue.text: Sees mind endlessly wandering, bringing downfall

indicators.note: letters that are wandering stray from their places, so they are rearranged
endlessly cuts off the final letter of mind

explanation.surface: Someone with a drifting, unfocused mind sees their ruin coming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' leaves MIN from mind; with SEES, 'wandering' rearranges SEESMIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Nemesis names an agent of retribution and so, by extension, a person's ruin or undoing.

clue.text: Pagan god takes a long time, being a bit twisted inside

indicators.note: a small twist inside the word shifts one interior letter to a new spot

parts.note: hours is used loosely for a long time, as in 'it took hours'

explanation.surface: A heathen deity is slow and somewhat warped within.
explanation.walkthrough: In HOURS the U moves one place right, past the R.
explanation.definitionFit: The falcon-headed sky deity of ancient Egypt, worshipped by non-Christians.

clue.text: Fish a fellow caught in European river, not hard

indicators.note: caught in means held inside, so the fellow goes within the river
not says the hard letter is dropped from the river

parts.note: the Rhine flows through Switzerland, Germany and the Netherlands
H is the pencil-lead abbreviation for hard
a gent is a gentleman, a fellow

explanation.surface: A man catches a fish in a European river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not hard' takes H from RHINE, leaving RINE, which holds A GENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Argentines are small silvery marine fish, also called herring smelts.

clue.text: Former Lib Dem leader sits by river thinking

indicators.note: sits by means is placed next to, so the leader follows the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and also one in Wales and England
Sir Menzies Campbell, Liberal Democrat leader 2006-07, was nicknamed Ming

explanation.surface: An ex-party leader sits pondering on a riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: Menzies is pronounced 'Mingis', hence the nickname Ming.
explanation.definitionFit: To deem is to judge or consider, so deeming is a form of considering.

clue.text: Poor man almost not bothering when kept outside game

indicators.note: almost means nearly all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: being lazy is not bothering to make an effort

indicators.note: kept outside means the when word encloses the game

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: A pauper idles about while a game is being played indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: RU, rugby union, is the usual crossword game; 'as' meaning 'when' is easy to miss.
explanation.definitionFit: In Jesus's parable, the beggar at the rich man's gate is the archetypal pauper.

clue.text: Characters in inn lazed around drinking fine wine

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so the scrambled letters swallow the fine letter
around means here and there, so the characters are mixed up

parts.note: F is the pencil abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: People lounging in a pub sip a good wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' rearranges INN LAZED; 'drinking' puts F inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A red grape grown chiefly in California and the wine made from it.

clue.text: Pitiful long-term prisoner given a place that's small in confinement

indicators.note: in confinement means locked up, so the prisoner holds the place

parts.note: Rudolf Hess was held in Spandau prison from 1947 until his death in 1987
PL is the short form of place, as in street names

explanation.surface: A lifer is given a cramped cell, a sad state of affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: an unlucky, wretched person is pitiable and unfortunate.

clue.text: Artist exhibited in courtyard behind house

indicators.note: behind means following, so the courtyard comes after the house

parts.note: a garth is an enclosed courtyard, as in a cloister

explanation.surface: A painter's work is on show in a yard behind a home.
explanation.definitionFit: William Hogarth, 18th-century English painter and engraver of A Rake's Progress.

clue.text: Settler has to map out territory briefly

parts.note: to map out a scheme is to plan it
Ter. is the short form of territory

explanation.surface: A colonist must survey the land quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: In history a planter was a colonist, as in the plantations of Ulster.

clue.text: Problem for sailors? Perceive distress, from what's reported

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so these words are heard rather than read

parts.note: to perceive something is to see it; to fret is to worry or be distressed

explanation.surface: A worried seaman spots trouble, judging by the reports.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea fret is a cold coastal fog off the sea, a hazard for anyone navigating.

clue.text: Thieves offering formula for getting small pieces

indicators.note: offering here means presenting the formula within the word for small pieces

parts.note: bits are small pieces
the formula is '...', so its joining word and is what sits inside to get the pieces

explanation.surface: Robbers offer a method for getting bits and pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as the formula 'B and ITS': B joined to ITS gives BITS, small pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: robbers or outlaws, especially armed ones.

clue.text: One who is lying may have this support close by

definitions.text: One who is lying may have this support close by

parts.words: One who is lying may have this support close by
parts.note: someone lying down in bed has the upright corner pillar of the bed nearby, not a liar

explanation.surface: A fibber may have a backer standing near.
explanation.walkthrough: Lying suggests telling untruths, but here it means lying in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: An upright post at a corner of a bed, supporting the frame or canopy.

clue.text: Home worker, good person engaged for very brief period

indicators.note: engaged means taken into the middle, so the good person goes inside

parts.note: in means at home
the ant is the crossword's usual worker insect
ST is the abbreviation for saint, a good person

explanation.surface: A domestic employee, a decent sort, is hired for a short stint.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a moment, the briefest span of time.

clue.text: That woman in Paris is embraced by reticent poet

indicators.note: embraced means held inside, so the French woman sits within the shy word

parts.note: reticent means shy and reserved
elle is French for she

explanation.surface: A Parisian woman is hugged by a bashful poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Percy Bysshe Shelley, English Romantic poet of Ozymandias.

clue.text: Donkey left occupying magnificent green countryside

indicators.note: occupying means sitting inside, so the donkey and left go within the magnificent word

parts.note: grand means splendid or magnificent
an ass is a donkey

explanation.surface: A donkey has wandered into splendid verdant fields.
explanation.definitionFit: Grassland is open grass-covered country, such as meadow or prairie.

clue.text: Conductor setting time in individual performances

indicators.note: in places the time letter inside the performances

parts.note: soli is the plural of solo, a performance by one

explanation.surface: A conductor sets the tempo during solo passages.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Georg Solti, Hungarian-British maestro who led the Chicago Symphony Orchestra.

clue.text: Passage is swamped by amber liquid

indicators.note: swamped by means flooded and surrounded, so the beer holds the little word

parts.note: ale is beer of an amber colour

explanation.surface: A corridor flooded with beer, perhaps after a pub mishap.
explanation.definitionFit: A walkway between rows of seats, as in a church or theatre.

clue.text: PM briefly entertained by bishop, a venomous type

indicators.note: being entertained by someone puts you inside their home, so the PM goes within

parts.note: RR, Right Reverend, is a bishop's title

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, losing the final letter

parts.note: Clement Attlee was British Prime Minister 1945-51

explanation.surface: A prime minister dines with a bishop who turns out to be poisonous company.
explanation.walkthrough: Bishop here is not B (chess) but RR, the Right Reverend title.
explanation.definitionFit: Rattler is an informal name for the rattlesnake, a poisonous American snake.

clue.text: Strange delivery that may fox the batsman?

definitions.text: Strange delivery that may fox the batsman?

parts.words: Strange delivery that may fox the batsman?
parts.note: the whole word means an eccentric

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler sends down a peculiar ball that bamboozles the batter.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a delivery is a ball bowled; split the answer in two to see the cricket reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a peculiar bowled ball; as one word it means an eccentric person.

clue.text: Beast straddling piano is a heavenly musician maybe

indicators.note: straddling means sitting astride, so the beast goes round the other letters

parts.note: a hart is a male deer
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: An animal sits astride a piano, an angelic performer perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Angels in heaven are traditionally pictured playing harps.

clue.text: Short narrated account not right as rendered by author

indicators.note: short means cut off before the end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a story narrated is told

indicators.note: not tells us to drop the right letter from the account

parts.note: a story is an account of events

explanation.surface: A brief tale, told inaccurately, as some writer might render it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' trims TOLD to TOL; 'not right' takes R from STORY, leaving STOY.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo Tolstoy, Russian novelist of War and Peace and Anna Karenina.
